title: Pentagon Data Breach Exposes SSNs and Military Records of Over 3 Million People
content_md: The Pentagon has confirmed a major breach involving a Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC) information system, exposing sensitive personal data belonging to more than three million people connected to the Department of Defense. The incident affected 2.76 million living individuals and approximately 294,000 deceased people, according to a U.S. defense official. The records included Social Security numbers , dates of birth, names, contact details, demographic data, and, in some cases, military occupational specialty information. Unauthorized users accessed the affected DMDC environment between October 2025 and July 2026. Officials said the intrusion stemmed from a vulnerability in a file-sharing system that allowed external users to access files stored on a vulnerable server. Pentagon Data Breach Exposes SSNs and Military Records DMDC discovered the issue on July 16, patched the flaw, restored the impacted system, and initiated privacy and cybersecurity incident-response procedures. The exposure is particularly serious because the compromised files reportedly contained unencrypted personally identifiable information. A notification letter reviewed by Military Times said the accessed data could include Social Security numbers alongside at least one additional identifier, such as a name, date of birth, contact information, race, sex, or military personnel information.
